craft_claim: A reflective passage may announce understanding only after the text has staged impasse and searching; declared epiphany without that staging reads as unearned, and premature verbal closure can block the very insight it imitates.

supporting_evidence.location: Annual Review of Psychology 65:71-93; abstract and antecedent-conditions sections
supporting_evidence.note: Reviews insight ('Aha!' solutions) as a distinct cognitive event with identifiable antecedents — preparation, impasse, and often a background incubation period — followed by a sudden restructuring of representation rather than a slow summation of effort.

supporting_evidence.location: Journal of Experimental Psychology: General 122(2):166-183; experiments on verbalization during incubation
supporting_evidence.note: Verbalizing an unresolved problem during incubation impairs subsequent solution of insight problems — language 'overshadows' insight — showing that premature verbal closure can displace the understanding it appears to report.

supporting_evidence.location: shared record in references/evidence/sources; cross-link claim clm-melodrama-unearned-emotion
supporting_evidence.note: Gardner's fit-to-stakes rule (emotion must not exceed what the situation has established) governs unearned display of feeling generally; understanding is one such display, so the shared melodrama claim extends to unearned epiphany.

counterevidence.note: Not all problem-solving is by insight — incremental analytic solution also exists, and some narrative understandings legitimately accumulate by summation; the claim targets understanding that appears with no prior impasse shown anywhere in the text.

scope: Reflective turns in all forms where a narrator reports arriving at meaning; not a ban on summarizing understanding in general.
exceptions: Aphoristic and maxim forms (epigram, counsel essay) state understanding as their premise; then the form, not the staging, must carry its authority — that is philosophical register, not reflective.
